method: Read .cursor/write-scope.json in the lane worktree to recover the audit-log path it declares: .cursor/.run/write-scope-audit.jsonl, relative to the hook process working directory.
Located every write-scope audit log on the filesystem. Exactly one exists, in the retired coordinator worktree /tmp/oe-root, last written 2026-08-27T04:56 by the coordinator's own probe.
Recorded its line count, then issued git status --porcelain, git rebase --abort and gh workflow list through the agent shell tool, covering both halves of the hooks.json matcher 'git|gh '.
Re-read the line count and searched the lane worktree for any audit file the hook would have created there.

commands_issued_through_the_agent_shell_.outcome: EXECUTED, returned 'fatal: No rebase in progress?'

root_cause: Cursor reads project hooks from the project root. The project root here is /workspace, whose checkout is the preserved CUR-01 evidence branch at 11a60dcf and does not contain .cursor/hooks.json at all. Every lane works in a git worktree under /tmp where hooks.json does exist and is never read. The hook scripts are correct and unreached.
stronger_than_the_coordinator_finding: The coordinator recorded that the hooks are read from the project root and the lanes are elsewhere. This run additionally establishes that the project-root checkout does not carry the hook definitions at all, so there is nothing at the only path Cursor consults. The failure is not a path mismatch that a cwd change would fix; the definitions are absent from the ref that is checked out there.
consequence_stated_plainly: Every boundary in .cursor/write-scope.json is documentation in this runtime. require_write_declaration: true cannot auto-refuse anything. Enforcement is voluntary and lane-side: write_admission.py refuses correctly when invoked by hand, and nothing invokes it.
why_no_mechanism_is_shipped_here: A fix belongs to whoever owns the runtime binding between the Cursor project root and the lane worktrees, not to a lane writing inside one worktree. Candidate mechanisms are recorded rather than invented: bind hooks at the project root ref that Cursor actually reads; or move lane execution into the project root; or replace the hook with a pre-push git hook installed per worktree, which fires where the write happens. Lane B declares this successor PENDING rather than closing the chain on a mechanism it did not ship.
candidate_mechanisms: Carry .cursor/hooks.json and .cursor/hooks/** onto whatever ref the Cursor project root checks out, so the only path Cursor consults is populated.
Install a per-worktree git pre-push hook that calls write_admission.py, which fires in the worktree where the push actually happens and does not depend on the provider reading a project root.
Keep enforcement lane-side but make it non-optional by having lane_guard.py refuse at integration any lane branch with no admitted write declaration recorded for its head.
